### What to Look for in Child Custody & Mediation Matters

1. **Accredited FDRP Status:** If you intend to file for parenting orders in the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia, you must legally attempt Family Dispute Resolution first (unless exceptions like domestic violence or urgency apply) and obtain a Section 60I Certificate. Ensure your chosen mediator is a registered FDRP.[[1]](https://www.michaellynchfamilylawyers.com.au/family-law-services/children/)[[2]](https://damiengreer.com.au/family-law/mediation/)
2. **Child-Inclusive vs. Child-Responsive Practice:** Ask whether the practitioner or lawyer advocates for child-inclusive mediation, which occasionally brings a child consultant into the mediation framework to ensure the child's psychological needs are safely represented.

If you can share:

- Whether you are looking for an **independent mediator** or a **lawyer to represent you** in negotiations
- Whether there are any **urgency or safety concerns** (such as a need for a Domestic Violence Order)
